newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM SAYS SEVERAL FACTORS PRESSURED AGROBANKA.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM SAYS SEVERAL FACTORS PRESSURED AGROBANKA.

text.p: Several factors -- including "non-collegial" behaviour among banks and the central bank's own monetary tightening -- contributed to liquidity problems at Agrobanka a.s. , Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said.

Speaking on Czech Radio on Tuesday, Klaus said Agrobanka, which the central bank last week put under "temporary" forced administration of an undetrmined length due to illiquidty, had to look at its own behaviour also as a source of its problems.

He said that the central bank's raising of its minimum reserve requirement for banks to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent earlier in the summer in an effort to reduce inflationary domestic demand, had played a role in Agrobanka's troubles.

"That affected the entire banking system and ... when someone is more injured and who has a fever and then breaks its leg, this is pretty, pretty bad. That's what happened also to Agrobanka," Klaus said in the radio interview.
Klaus said Agrobanka "acted maybe riskier, in some ways, maybe less riskier, maybe smarter, maybe it made more mistakes", but said the bank's behaviour played a role.

The Czech National Bank had said the interbank market had recently ignored trading with Agrobanka, which had close connections with the failed Kreditni Banka a.s. through its shareholder, the investment group Motoinvest.
Klaus said that "such non-collegiality between banks added another drop to the whole problem".
The prime minister, who has been praised for his classical liberal free-market views, defended the intervention by the central bank in Agrobanka saying liberalism does not mean "insufficient order".
